items.headline: September US CPI runs hot (3.7% y/y, core 2.6% y/y), reviving Fed hike odds
items.summary: Headline CPI rose 0.6% m/m / 3.7% y/y and core CPI rose 0.3% m/m / 2.6% y/y, both topping consensus on the annualized measures. The print pushed Oct 27-28 FOMC hike odds from ~22% to 40-55% and sent 10-year yields toward 5.19-5.33% and the dollar to an 18-month high.
items.actionable: The direct cause of Wednesday's selloff across the book's equity, gold and silver legs at once -- the hawkish-Fed repricing is the single biggest near-term risk to the levered silver/miners sleeve; today's 20:30 SGT PPI/Retail Sales/Philly Fed prints are the next test of whether it broadens.

items.headline: Gold and silver tumble as hot CPI boosts rate-hike bets
items.summary: Silver fell -6.11% (SLV) and gold fell -1.49% (GLD), driven by higher real yields and a stronger dollar after the hot CPI print raised the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metals. Miners (GDX -4.40%, SILJ -5.90%, SLVP -5.91%) fell even harder than spot.
items.actionable: Direct hit to the book's core levered-silver thesis (1.79x leverage) -- the drop looks rate-driven rather than demand-driven, but the survivability/margin-call distance on the levered silver leg should be re-checked against today's close before adding exposure.

items.headline: KOSPI crashes 5.46% on 'Black Tuesday' as Chinese memory maker CXMT stokes competition fears
items.summary: Samsung Electronics fell 7.4% and SK Hynix fell ~10% after reports that China's ChangXin Memory Technologies will launch next-gen server DRAM within the year, reviving memory-oversupply/competition fears. The selloff spread to the Nikkei and TSMC, pressuring sentiment across Asian chip-exposed names including SMIC.
items.actionable: A genuine competitive catalyst (not just macro sympathy) for the book's SMIC (0981.HK) exposure -- Korea's foreign-selling streak in chip megacaps is concentrated, not broad, so watch for whether it spreads to HK-listed semis specifically rather than assuming contagion.

items.headline: Energy Fuels drops ~10% on $500M ATM share-sale filing, drags uranium/nuclear peers
items.summary: Energy Fuels filed to authorize up to $500 million in new share sales via an at-the-market program, raising dilution concerns and sending the stock to a 52-week low near $8.34. The decline spread across uranium/nuclear-adjacent names (Oklo -5%, NuScale -7%, Centrus -5%) as 10-year yields climbed.
items.actionable: A financing-structure catalyst, not a change in the rare-earth thesis -- sell-side Strong Buy ratings on UUUU were unmoved by the filing, which argues against reflexively cutting the rare-earth watchlist names on today's price action alone.

items.headline: Xiaomi shares jump on SkyNomad EV order strength, extending gains into Oct 14
items.summary: Xiaomi stock surged (+8-9% on Oct 9, +5.35% on Oct 14) after disclosing more than 70,000 non-refundable orders for its SkyNomad SUV in its first month, plus delivery of over 10,000 units in September -- the company's strongest monthly EV delivery figure of 2026.
items.actionable: Xiaomi (1810.HK) is the one bright spot in an otherwise ugly day for the HK tech sleeve -- a genuine company-specific catalyst (EV order momentum) rather than a macro or sector read, and it diverges from Tencent/SMIC's declines the same session.

items.headline: Hormuz tanker attacks surge to wartime-high frequency
items.summary: Ships are being struck in the Strait of Hormuz nearly every day this month, with at least 12 tankers attacked in a single week and six vessels hit on Oct 11 alone; Iran's IRGC has deployed new surveillance units and threatened any tanker ignoring its 'rules.' About 25% of global seaborne oil trade transits the strait.
items.actionable: The Gulf War premium (~$20/bbl per Goldman) is the reason oil held up even as the rest of the risk complex sold off Wednesday -- a genuine hedge characteristic worth remembering if considering energy exposure against the book's silver/gold-heavy risk sleeve.

items.headline: Houthis strike Aramco HQ; Riyadh airport shut through Oct 17
items.summary: Houthi forces claimed an attack on Saudi Aramco's administrative building in Dhahran on Oct 13, a day after a Saudi-led coalition strike on a Houthi fuel depot in Sanaa. Separately, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remains suspended through Oct 17 after a wave of missile/drone strikes on Saudi airports killed at least 20 people since Oct 6.
items.actionable: Escalation risk is rising, not fading -- continue to treat the oil geopolitical premium as a live, widening risk rather than a one-off spike when sizing any energy or broad-commodity exposure.

items.headline: Lynas to build Brazil rare-earth separation plant, advances Meteoric acquisition
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths announced plans for a rare-earth oxide separation plant in Minas Gerais, Brazil -- potentially one of the largest outside China -- tied to its AUD 968 million all-share acquisition of Meteoric Resources (agreed Oct 1), which adds 802,000 tonnes of NdPr oxide reserves. The stock nonetheless touched a 52-week low amid the broader rare-earth/uranium rout.
items.actionable: A genuine ex-China-supply-chain positive for the rare-earth watchlist even as the stock sells off on sector sympathy -- Lynas fell far less than MP/UUUU this week (-0.86% vs -5.84%/-10%), consistent with the news being read as a long-term positive.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls to ~$81,500 as hot CPI lifts Fed hike odds to 55%
items.summary: Bitcoin fell roughly 2% to near $81,524, with Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin also down over 2%, as the hot inflation print pushed October Fed-hike odds from ~21% to 55% and triggered about $331.9 million in liquidations. Spot BTC/ETH ETFs still posted net inflows despite the price drop.
items.actionable: Not a book holding, but a read-through on risk appetite: crypto selling off in lockstep with gold/silver/equities on the same rate shock reinforces that this is a single macro story (hawkish Fed), not an asset-class-specific one.

items.headline: CCC-rated high-yield spreads widen to 4-year highs even as broader credit stays calm
items.summary: The ICE BofA CCC & Below US High Yield OAS rose to ~12.1-12.5%, surpassing the April 2025 peak of 11.4% and hitting its highest level since November 2022. The stress is concentrated in the weakest-rated credits only -- the broader BB/B high-yield spread remains a calm ~3.15% -- suggesting idiosyncratic rather than systemic credit risk so far.
items.actionable: Worth monitoring rather than acting on today -- if CCC stress broadens into broad HY, that would be a genuine systemic warning sign for the book's risk sleeve; for now it is narrow and not yet actionable.

items.headline: AirTrunk shelves Singapore REIT IPO amid market volatility
items.summary: Blackstone-backed data-centre operator AirTrunk postponed its planned ~US$1.5 billion Singapore REIT listing until 2026/2027, citing higher interest rates and market volatility. S-REITs are down 8.2% YTD even as the broader STI is up 22.9%.
items.actionable: A read-through for the book's SGX REIT sleeve (MPACT, Keppel REIT, CICT) -- higher-for-longer rates after today's hot CPI are the same headwind that shelved this IPO, reinforcing caution on REIT-heavy SGX exposure near-term.

items.headline: Tencent raises $5.7 billion in debt sale despite AI-spending scrutiny
items.summary: Tencent Holdings sold about $5.7 billion in US dollar and offshore yuan bonds, drawing combined orders exceeding $23 billion even as global AI-capex concerns weighed on markets. Proceeds are earmarked for general corporate purposes amid rising AI infrastructure investment.
items.actionable: Strong demand (>4x oversubscribed) for Tencent's bond sale is a credit-market vote of confidence that sits alongside Wednesday's modest equity decline (-0.42%) -- the book's Tencent position looks comparatively resilient versus SMIC/Korea's chip-sector stress this week.
